newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Denel wants arms exports up 20 pct p.a.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Denel wants arms exports up 20 pct p.a.

text.p: South Africa's state-owned arms manufacturer Denel said on Thursday it wants to increase the value of its exports by at least a fifth each year.

Acting managing director Seshi Chonco told a news conference that Denel, which has diversified into non-military production since the end of apartheid, made a profit of 379 million rand ($80.6 million) on three billion rand turnover in the year to March 1996.
Exports during the same period, the most recent for which figures have been made available, accounted for 30 percent of revenue, up from 16 percent three years before.
"We'd like to see them grow by 20 percent a year at least," Denel's marketing director Andrew Tonkin said.
Chonco said Denel's share of the global arms trade was 0.4 percent.
South African arms exports have been hindered by a legal wrangle with the United States over past sales that broke an apartheid-era embargo.

The row has now been settled and Ron Haywood, chief executive of the state arms procurement and export promotion agency Armscor, told a separate news conference he hoped trade with the United States could restart once a compliance manual, the one remaining obstacle, was finalised.
He said he hoped this could happen by September.
South African arms exports are worth around one billion rand a year. Denel is the largest manufacturer but defence industry companies number around 700.
